html:
Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai was a Sufi poet and saint of Sindh, born in 1689, who lived at Bhit Shah, north of Hyderabad, and is counted the greatest poet in the Sindhi language.

His poems were collected after his death as Shah Jo Risalo. They retell old Sindhi folk tales of lovers such as Sassui and Punhun and Umar Marvi, and use their longing as a picture of the soul's search for God. He set them to his own musical modes, and he is said to have devised a new stringed instrument, the tambooro.

His shrine at Bhit Shah holds a festival each year, and his verses are still sung there every night. Like Bulleh Shah in Punjab, he wrote in the people's language rather than Persian, in the tradition of Sufism. Sindhi nationalists see him as the soul of their culture.
